title: ProPublica: DOJ Blocked Civil Rights Charges Against ICE Agent; Prosecutor Fired After Speaking Out
excerpt: ProPublica revealed that DOJ leadership in Washington blocked federal prosecutors in Minnesota from charging ICE agent Christian Castro with deprivation of rights under color of law, instead directing a lesser false-statements charge — a decision the lead prosecutor said he fought with his "strongest possible" objections before being fired.
content:
ProPublica reported on September 3, 2026, that Department of Justice leaders in Washington, D.C., quashed plans by Minnesota federal prosecutors to bring civil rights charges against ICE agent Christian Castro under the deprivation of rights under color of law statute — the same charge used against officers convicted in the killing of George Floyd.

  • Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Evans, the lead prosecutor on the case, wrote in an email to victims' lawyers that DOJ leadership had directed him to charge Castro "only with False Statements" — a charge carrying significantly lighter penalties.
  • Evans wrote: "This is being directed by the Main Justice and the US Attorney. I objected in the strongest possible terms and fought it as hard as I could. It wasn't enough."
  • After ProPublica published Evans's email, he was fired from the DOJ. Sources said he was then placed under investigation for alleged obstruction of a grand jury investigation.
  • Castro's attorney and DOJ officials declined comment; DOJ said the civil rights investigation was still ongoing and no final determination had been made.

The episode drew bipartisan criticism and underscored concerns that the Justice Department under the Trump administration was shielding ICE agents from accountability for actions taken during immigration enforcement operations, even when career prosecutors believed civil rights violations had occurred.
